rv.q: It’s hard to watch and occasionally repugnant, but it makes a compelling case for the distinctiveness of Kane’s vision — uncompromising, ugly, cruel and intoxicating.
Her production is simultaneously repellent and compelling.
Kane's play is not quite brilliant: it feels more like a series of short sharp sensations rather than a fully realised drama.
I’ve rarely been so overwhelmed by a show, but I’ve also never longed so much for one to end.
My particular problem is that such relentless exposure to man’s inhumanity to man produces a sense of fatigue rather than of horror.
Katie Mitchell’s production does not ritualise or disguise any of this.
And Cleansed is Kane at her most utterly uncompromising.
If Cleansed is like a tooth being pulled, A Girl Is a Half Formed Thing is a slow, silent descent into despair, a beautiful, choking sob of a play crowned by a truly exceptional performance.

cn.t: Critics are divided on Katie Mitchell's revival of Kane's brutal 1998 play—some find it compellingly visceral, others numbing. The unflinching staging earns respect, but reactions range from intoxicated to depleted.
